description:
The Kura server the operator pushes `KuraTenant` and `KuraVault` to.
Cluster-scoped: one server serves the cluster. `Ready` tells whether the
server answers and accepts the operator's identity.

auth.description:
How the operator proves who it is to the server. Required: the server
accepts the documents from one configured identity only.

serviceAccountToken.description:
A projected ServiceAccount token, rotated by the kubelet, that the
server verifies against the cluster's OIDC issuer. No secret at rest.

audience.description: The token's audience, equal to the server's `documents.operator.audience`.

tls.description: How the operator verifies the server's TLS certificate (`https` only).

caSecretRef.description:
Optional custom CA certificate to verify the instance's TLS with,
read from a Kubernetes `Secret` (the referenced `key` must hold a PEM
bundle). Use this to trust a private CA without mounting it into the
operator pod — the operator reads the Secret via the API and hands the
PEM to its HTTP client. It is added *on top of* the platform trust
store, so publicly-signed endpoints keep working. When unset, only the
platform trust store (plus the usual `SSL_CERT_FILE`/`SSL_CERT_DIR`
env vars) is used.

insecureSkipVerify.description:
Skip certificate verification entirely — insecure, intended only for
throwaway/self-signed instances. Prefer `caSecretRef` below, which
trusts a private CA without turning verification off.

url.description:
Base URL of the Kura server's API, such as `http://kura.kura.svc:8080`.
Use `https` for anything that leaves the node.
